sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Pierce County?
sections.html:
The Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer's Office sets the value of your property and also collects the tax, so one office handles both the number on your assessment notice and the payment. It works from 2401 South 35th Street, Room 142, in Tacoma, and is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Pierce County Finance, at 1501 Market St., Suite 120, takes payments on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

Pierce County was formed out of Thurston County on December 22, 1852, and is named for President Franklin Pierce. Tacoma is the county seat and largest city. The county covers about 1,805 square miles, from Puget Sound up to Mount Rainier, the highest point in Washington at 14,410 feet. The Census Bureau estimates 946,288 residents as of July 1, 2025, which makes Pierce the second most populous county in the state behind King County.

Cities inside the county include Tacoma, Puyallup, Lakewood, University Place, Gig Harbor, Bonney Lake and Sumner, and parts of Auburn, Enumclaw, Milton and Pacific reach into it. A house in any of them is billed by the same county office.

  • Phone for assessment and tax questions: (253) 798-6111.
  • Automated payment and balance line: (253) 798-3333, with your parcel number ready.
  • Mail checks payable to Pierce County, with the remittance stub or parcel number, to Pierce County Finance, P.O. Box 11621, Tacoma, WA 98411-6621.
  • Card and e-check payments run through an outside vendor that adds 2.35% for credit cards, $0.50 per e-check and $3.50 per debit card.

sections.h2: What does the Pierce County housing market look like for a seller?
sections.html:
Pierce County is mostly a place where people own their homes: the Census Bureau puts the owner-occupied rate at 64.7% for 2020 to 2024, with 382,172 housing units counted for July 2025. The median value of an owner-occupied home was $526,600 over that period, median household income was $99,564, and the average commute was 31.3 minutes. About a quarter of workers commute to King County.

Joint Base Lewis-McChord is the largest public employer, supporting roughly 60,000 military and civilian jobs. MultiCare Health System and Virginia Mason Franciscan Health run the two largest hospitals. Mount Rainier last erupted between 1820 and 1854, and a lahar warning system for the Puyallup River valley has operated since 1998.

sections.h2: When are Pierce County property taxes due, and what happens if I pay late?
sections.html:
Pierce County property tax is due in two halves: the first half by April 30 and the second half by October 31. Because October 31 fell on a Saturday in 2026, the county moved the second-half deadline to Monday, November 2, and that date has now passed. If your second half is unpaid today, call the office for the exact amount owed with interest.

State law lets you pay in halves when the bill is $50 or more. Late payments carry interest figured monthly from the date of delinquency under RCW 84.56.020. For a residence with four or fewer units, the county charges 0.75% per month (9% a year) on the full-year tax starting May 1, and state law bars penalties on those homes. Other property, such as larger apartment buildings and personal property, pays 1% per month plus penalties.

DateWhat happens
April 30First half is due.
May 1Interest starts on the full-year tax if the first half is unpaid: 0.75% per month on homes of one to four units for tax year 2023 and later, 1% per month on other property.
June 1Three percent penalty on other property.
October 31 (November 2 in 2026)Second half is due.
December 1Additional eight percent penalty on other property, for an 11% total.

Source: Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer FAQ and RCW 84.56.020.

If no statement reaches you by March 31 and a mortgage company does not pay your taxes, call (253) 798-6111 for a copy.

sections.h2: How does Pierce County value my house?
sections.html:
Washington law requires the Assessor-Treasurer to value property at 100% of true and fair market value every year, defined as the price a willing buyer would pay a willing seller. The value follows the market, so assessed values fall when prices fall and rise when prices rise. The county names neighborhood desirability, building costs and improvements you have made as factors.

Each property is inspected about once every six years under a revaluation plan approved by the Washington Department of Revenue. Inspections can come sooner after new construction, a board case, an appraisal review, a sales verification or a split of the parcel. You may refuse private access, but you may not deny it to the assessor or staff, and you can confirm a staff member's credentials at (253) 798-6111.

The county's November 2026 notice put countywide taxes at almost $2.1 billion, which fund schools, libraries, parks and emergency services.

sections.h2: How do I appeal my Pierce County assessment?
sections.html:
You appeal to the Pierce County Board of Equalization on or before July 1 of the assessment year, or within 60 days of the date a value change notice was mailed, whichever is later. Call the board at (253) 798-7415 to get the appeal form. State law, RCW 84.40.038, also lets a board waive a late filing for good cause.

The county is clear about what counts. You must give specific reasons why the assessor's number differs from market value (RCW 84.40.0301). The size of the increase, personal hardship, the amount of the tax and other matters unrelated to market value cannot be considered. Good cause for a late petition under RCW 84.40.038 includes the following.

  • Death or serious illness of the taxpayer or close family.
  • Wrong written advice on filing from board or assessor staff.
  • A natural disaster such as a flood or earthquake.
  • A postal delay documented by the Postal Service.

sections.h2: What tax relief can Pierce County seniors and people with disabilities use?
sections.html:
Pierce County runs two programs, an exemption that lowers the tax and a deferral that postpones it. The exemption is expanding: starting January 2027, more homeowners who are 61 or older, or who have a qualifying disability, will see their bills reduced. For 2026 the county lists these requirements for the new tier.

  • Owned and lived in the home for at least six months in 2026.
  • Turned 61 in 2026, or a veteran with at least a 40% disability rating, or a taxpayer with a qualifying disability who did not serve.
  • Combined household income of $85,000 or less for 2026, with a standard deduction for items such as medical premiums and prescription drugs.

Owners who met the earlier rules in 2023, 2024 or 2025 can still apply and could receive a refund. For those years the county lists income up to $64,000 and a veteran rating of at least 80%.

The deferral is separate. Applicants must apply every year, be at least 60 on December 31 of the application year and stay under an annual income of $68,319 per the county page. The Department of Revenue pays the county on your behalf, and the amount becomes a lien that is repaid with interest when ownership transfers (RCW 84.38).

sections.h2: How are property taxes handled when I sell a Pierce County house?
sections.html:
Property tax is a lien on the parcel from January 1 of the year it is levied, and RCW 84.60.020 says that when the sale contract is silent, the seller covers the share of the year before the closing date and the buyer covers the rest. In practice the escrow officer prorates the bill, and any unpaid balance, interest or deferral is paid out of the seller's proceeds. Ask for a payoff figure before you accept an offer.

The seller also usually pays the state real estate excise tax, which is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale. For sales beginning January 1, 2027, the state portion is 1.1% on the first $551,000 of price, 1.28% from $551,000 to $1,551,000, 2.75% from there to $3,051,000 and 3% above that, with the local share added on top. On a sale at the county's $526,600 median value, the state portion would be about $5,793.

A senior exemption does not have to be lost in a move. RCW 84.36.381 allows a claimant who sells or is displaced to transfer exemption status to a replacement residence, though no one may receive the exemption on more than one home in a year.

sections.h2: What happens if I am behind on Pierce County property taxes?
sections.html:
Foreclosure for unpaid taxes is slow. Under RCW 84.64.050, the treasurer issues certificates of delinquency only after three years have passed from the date of delinquency, and no certificate may be filed when the unpaid tax is $100 or less. The owner and anyone with a recorded interest gets notice and has thirty days to appear or pay the amount due.

Before that point there are options. The treasurer may offer a payment agreement or accept partial payments. Near the three-year mark the treasurer must waive outstanding interest and penalties for an income-qualified owner who lives in the home and has not received a waiver before (RCW 84.56.020). Payments aimed at avoiding foreclosure go to the Assessor-Treasurer's Office, Attention: Foreclosure Avoidance, 2401 South 35th Street, Room 142, Tacoma, WA 98409-1498.

If back taxes make keeping the house impractical, ask the treasurer for a payoff figure and have your escrow officer pay it from the sale proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: When is the second half of Pierce County property tax due in 2026?
faqs.a: The deadline was Monday, November 2, 2026, because October 31 fell on a weekend. That date has passed, so call (253) 798-6111 for the balance including interest on any unpaid amount.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Pierce County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor-Treasurer's Office at (253) 798-6111. To request an appeal form, call the Pierce County Board of Equalization at (253) 798-7415.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal if July 1 has gone by?
faqs.a: Yes, if you received a value change notice, because the deadline is the later of July 1 or 60 days after it was mailed. A board may also accept a late petition for good cause.

faqs.q: Does the senior exemption follow me to a new home?
faqs.a: It can. RCW 84.36.381 lets a person who sells or is displaced transfer exemption status to a replacement residence, with no more than one exempt home per year.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax at closing in Pierce County?
faqs.a: If the contract says nothing, the seller owes the share of the year before the sale date and the buyer owes the rest. Your escrow officer normally prorates the bill.
